urnfield-culture.name: Urnfield culture
urnfield-culture.summary: A late Bronze Age culture of Central Europe, roughly 1300–750 BC, named for its practice of burying cremated ashes in urns in fields.

vicia-faba.name: Horse bean
vicia-faba.summary: A hardier variety of the broad or fava bean with smaller, harder seeds, typically fed to horses and other animals rather than eaten by people.

salzkammergut.name: Salzkammergut
salzkammergut.summary: A resort region in Austria stretching east from the city of Salzburg, whose name means 'salt domain' after salt mines administered there from 1745 to 1850.

bell-beaker-culture.name: Bell Beaker culture
bell-beaker-culture.summary: A Bronze Age archaeological culture named for its inverted-bell drinking vessel, spreading across Western Europe from around 2800 BCE.

n-tice-culture.name: Únětice culture
n-tice-culture.summary: An archaeological culture at the start of the Central European Bronze Age, dated to about 2300 to 1600 BC, known from sites across the Czech Republic, Slovakia, Poland and Germany.

corded-ware-culture.name: Corded Ware culture
corded-ware-culture.summary: A broad European archaeological culture from about 2900 to 2300 BC, likely descended from Yamnaya migrants and a probable vector for spreading Indo-European languages.

bronocice.name: Bronocice
bronocice.summary: Village in south-central Poland where a pot was found in 1976 bearing the earliest known image of a wheeled vehicle, dated to about 3635 to 3370 BC.

hallstatt.name: Hallstatt
hallstatt.summary: A small Austrian town known since prehistoric times for salt production, which gave its name to the Hallstatt archaeological culture.

nebra-sky-disc.name: Nebra sky disc
nebra-sky-disc.summary: A Bronze Age bronze disc inlaid with gold symbols of the sun, moon, and stars, found near Nebra, Germany in 1999 and dated to about 1800 to 1600 BC; the oldest known depiction of astronomical phenomena.

pleiades.name: Pleiades
pleiades.summary: An open star cluster in the constellation Taurus, about 444 light-years away, the brightest star cluster visible to the naked eye and known since antiquity as the Seven Sisters.

memory-of-the-world-programme.name: Memory of the World Register
memory-of-the-world-programme.summary: A UNESCO register recognizing documentary heritage of global importance, aiming to protect archives and collections from loss, decay or destruction.

gold-hat.name: Gold hats
gold-hat.summary: Four known cone-shaped Bronze Age European artifacts, made of thin sheet gold worn over tall conical headdresses, dated to roughly 1400–800 BC.

hallstatt-culture.name: Hallstatt culture
hallstatt-culture.summary: A Western and Central European archaeological culture spanning the Late Bronze Age through Early Iron Age (12th-6th centuries BC), commonly linked to Proto-Celtic peoples.

nordic-bronze-age.name: Nordic Bronze Age
nordic-bronze-age.summary: A period of Scandinavian prehistory from about 2000/1750 to 500 BC, shaped by Central European metalworking traditions and maintaining trade links with Mycenaean Greece.

metonic-cycle.name: Metonic cycle
metonic-cycle.summary: A roughly 19-year cycle after which lunar phases recur on the same calendar dates, identified by the Greek astronomer Meton of Athens in the 5th century BCE and used in lunisolar calendars.

trundholm-sun-chariot.name: Trundholm sun chariot
trundholm-sun-chariot.summary: A Nordic Bronze Age bronze statue of a horse pulling a large disc on wheels, discovered in Denmark in 1902 and now held at the National Museum of Denmark.

tollense-valley-battlefield.name: Tollense valley battlefield
tollense-valley-battlefield.summary: A Bronze Age battlefield in northern Germany where an estimated 4,000 warriors fought in the 13th century BC, discovered in 1996 and still under excavation; the largest known Bronze Age battle site.

mecklenburg-vorpommern.name: Mecklenburg-Vorpommern
mecklenburg-vorpommern.summary: A coastal German state formed in 1945 from the historic regions of Mecklenburg and Western Pomerania, dissolved in 1952 and re-established in 1990 after reunification.

tollense.name: Tollense
tollense.summary: River in Mecklenburg-Vorpommern in northeastern Germany, about 96 km long. It is a right tributary of the Peene.

neustrelitz.name: Neustrelitz
neustrelitz.summary: A German town on the Zierker See that served as capital of the Duchy of Mecklenburg-Strelitz from 1738 to 1918.

p-mmelte.name: Pömmelte
p-mmelte.summary: A village in Germany, now part of the town Barby, where prehistoric dwelling structures dating from 2800 to 2200 BC, linked to the Bell Beaker and Unetice cultures, have been identified.

funnelbeaker-culture.name: Funnelbeaker culture
funnelbeaker-culture.summary: A Neolithic archaeological culture in north-central Europe, about 4100 to 2800 BCE, that brought farming and husbandry to pottery-using hunter-gatherers north of the Elbe and Vistula rivers.

schifferstadt.name: Schifferstadt
schifferstadt.summary: Town in Rhineland-Palatinate, Germany, near Ludwigshafen and Speyer; the only urban municipality in its district besides Ludwigshafen itself.

avanton.name: Avanton
avanton.summary: A commune in western France, near where a Bronze Age golden hat known as the Avanton Gold Cone was found in 1844.

sch-nebeck.name: Schönebeck
sch-nebeck.summary: Town on the Elbe near Magdeburg, Germany, once noted for a large salt mine; nearby prehistoric circular enclosures were built around 2300 BC.

tumulus-culture.name: Tumulus culture
tumulus-culture.summary: The dominant material culture of Central Europe during the Middle Bronze Age, around 1600 to 1300 BC, succeeding the Unetice culture and later replaced by the Urnfield culture.

trassem.name: Trassem
trassem.summary: A small municipality in Germany's Rhineland-Palatinate region, in the Trier-Saarburg district.

trzciniec-culture.name: Trzciniec culture
trzciniec-culture.summary: An Early and Middle Bronze Age archaeological culture, dated 2400 to 1300 BC, found mainly in Poland and parts of Lithuania.
